scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO develops next-generation AI agent architectures powered by LLMs, focused on autonomous planning, tool use, and goal-directed action based on high-level instructions.

MAESTRO develops a hybrid neuro-symbolic planning engine that decomposes high-level goals into executable sub-task graphs with formally specified pre-conditions, post-conditions, and verification checkpoints; integrates search-based planning algorithms (Monte Carlo Tree Search, hierarchical task networks) with LLM-driven heuristic evaluation; and supports self-correction through plan monitoring and replanning from verified intermediate states.

MAESTRO designs a unified memory architecture integrating working memory (short-term, attention-managed), episodic memory (retrieval-augmented experience store), and semantic memory (persistent knowledge graph), managed by a memory controller balancing recall accuracy against computational cost.

MAESTRO develops an External Tool and API Orchestration Layer providing a typed tool registry with capability model, formal tool selection and invocation policies, standardised API adapters abstracting heterogeneous protocols (REST, GraphQL, HL7 FHIR, OPC-UA), post-invocation verification and grounding, execution monitoring with fallback/recovery, and auditable tool execution traces — positioned as the architectural mechanism to overcome limitations of large AI models in tasks requiring accuracy and reliability.

MAESTRO enhances agent autonomy through self-planning and self-optimization via the planning engine's self-correction capabilities — detecting execution failures and replanning from verified intermediate states rather than restarting from scratch.

MAESTRO advances memory-augmented AI agents for robust long-term reasoning and lifelong learning through a unified memory architecture enabling experience-based learning (episodic memory), persistent domain knowledge (semantic memory), and context-aware agent behaviour over extended interactions.

MAESTRO develops advanced multi-agent frameworks for collaborative heterogeneous agents, including formal task-delegation protocols with provable convergence guarantees, conflict resolution mechanisms, and auditable delegation and negotiation traces — constituting research on AI agent frameworks based on mixed AI architectures.

MAESTRO incorporates qualitative and quantitative KPIs, standardised benchmarking across all demonstrators, and structured progress monitoring at 6-month integration checkpoints, with measurable performance targets benchmarked against operational baselines and current state-of-the-art agent systems.
The project will link to the resources offered by AI Factories, including Data Labs, for compute-intensive training and evaluation.

All research outputs — frameworks, models, benchmarks, the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, and demonstrator results — will be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform.
MAESTRO allocates dedicated tasks for cohesion activities with ADRA (European Partnership on AI, Data and Robotics) and the GenAI4EU central Hub (CSA HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18).

MAESTRO validates its research in two call-identified Apply AI sectors: healthcare (clinical decision support system using HL7 FHIR API integration, specialist sub-agents, and autonomous diagnostic reasoning) and advanced manufacturing (multi-agent process optimisation with OPC-UA industrial connectors, digital twin APIs, and sensor data streams).

MAESTRO includes a cross-sector logistics and supply chain transfer demonstrator — coordinating operations across warehouses, carriers, and customs with connectors to logistics tracking systems, customs clearance APIs, and carrier scheduling interfaces — explicitly positioned as demonstrating architecture portability beyond the three call-named Apply AI sectors.
scope_findings.flag_reason: Logistics and supply chain is not one of the three Apply AI sectors named in SR-16 (healthcare, advanced manufacturing, in-vehicle autonomous driving), and no Tier 2B scope element in scope_requirements.json or call_constraints.json explicitly confirms logistics as an in-scope demonstrator sector for this call topic. The concept note itself positions this demonstrator as going 'beyond the call's specifically identified Apply AI sectors,' acknowledging it falls outside the named scope boundary. While the general AI agent research scope (SR-01, SR-07) does not explicitly exclude logistics, and the logistics demonstrator supplements rather than substitutes the two named-sector demonstrators, the partial overlap with SR-16 and the explicit admission in the concept note that logistics exceeds the call's named sectors requires this claim to be flagged. Resolution depends on whether evaluators accept cross-sector generalisation as positively contributing to the portfolio or as a scope extension requiring further justification.

scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO assesses the transferability of its architecture to in-vehicle autonomous driving settings through a targeted architectural mapping analysis (WP8) but does not conduct a full demonstrator in this sector; the strategic positioning explicitly acknowledges the consortium lacks automotive sector partners.
scope_findings.flag_reason: In-vehicle autonomous driving is one of the three priority sectors named in SR-16 and targeted by the portfolio coverage mechanism in CC-09, which is designed to ensure at least one funded proposal focuses on each of the three sectors. MAESTRO addresses this sector only via an architectural mapping analysis (WP8), not as a primary demonstrator sector. This partial coverage may not constitute 'focusing on' in-vehicle autonomous driving in the sense intended by CC-09, and may affect MAESTRO's positioning under the portfolio coverage procedure for that sector. The strategic positioning document is transparent about this limitation. Evaluators must assess whether the architectural mapping analysis constitutes sufficient sector relevance under CC-09. The flag does not reflect an exclusion of autonomous driving from the topic's scope, but a concern about whether the level of engagement satisfies the portfolio coverage intent.

scope_findings.claim: Demonstrator results will be validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities (TEFs) and further disseminated and deployed via European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs).

MAESTRO's open-source framework and standardised agent interaction protocols will lower barriers for European SMEs and startups to build on next-generation AI agent technology, strengthening the European AI ecosystem's competitiveness and reducing strategic dependency on non-European AI platforms.
scope_findings.flag_reason: No Tier 2B scope element in scope_requirements.json (SR-01 through SR-16) or call_constraints.json (CC-01 through CC-14) directly identifies SME barrier reduction, European AI ecosystem competitiveness strengthening, or strategic dependency reduction as an in-scope research or demonstrator claim for this call topic. SR-13 (build on relevant projects and develop synergies with initiatives) and SR-16 (Apply AI relevance) partially relate to ecosystem engagement but do not confirm this specific claim as within the topic's declared scope boundary. Per constitutional constraint 1, a claim cannot be assessed as in_scope without a traceable match to a Tier 2B scope element; there is no such match for this claim. It may be appropriate as a broader societal or economic impact assertion in the Impact section of the proposal, but it requires either a specific Tier 2B grounding or explicit framing as an anticipated outcome rather than a core project scope claim.

scope_findings.claim: Activities start at TRL 2 and MAESTRO targets TRL 5 validation by end of the project across both call-identified Apply AI sector demonstrators.

scope_findings.flag_reason: The claimed 48-month project duration aligns with CC-13 (maximum 48 months), but CC-13 carries status 'Assumed' with an explicit assumption_note in call_constraints.json requiring verification against Horizon Europe General Annex B. The topic-specific call extract documents are silent on project duration; 48 months is noted as the standard maximum for large RIA actions but has not been Confirmed from the topic text itself. The 48-month duration claim cannot be confirmed as compliant with the call's constraints until CC-13 is verified from General Annex B. This flag does not indicate the claimed duration is out-of-scope, but that the constraint basis is unconfirmed at Tier 2B.

tier_authority_applied: Tier 2B scope_requirements.json (docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/scope_requirements.json; 16 scope requirement entries SR-01 through SR-16, all status Confirmed); Tier 2B call_constraints.json (docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/call_constraints.json; 14 constraint entries CC-01 through CC-14, status Confirmed except CC-13 which is Assumed). No other scope authority consulted. No generic programme knowledge used as substitute for or extension of Tier 2B source data.
